text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto implicated President Farooq Leghari in the murder of her brother, Murtaza Bhutto, who was killed by the police in a shootout in Karachi on September 20.
- Three more ministers were sworn into the caretaker cabinet of Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.
- The provincial assembly of North Western Frontier Province was dissolved by the governor on the advice of President Farooq Leghari.
- Sources said six top bureaucrats and two federal ministers of the ousted government may be taken into protective custody on Thursday on charges of corruption.
- Nine ministers were inducted into the cabinet of caretaker Sindh province Chief Minister Mumtaz Bhutto.
- India said it was ready to discuss contentious bilateral issues with Pakistan but urged Islamabad to prepare the right environment for it.
- All banks will revert to a six-day working week from Saturday after the government decision to abolish the two-day holiday, bankers said.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid assured business leaders that he will them take into confidence on his government's economic policies.
- A high-powered IMF delegation, headed by Paul Chabrier, the IMF's Middle East director, is arriving in Islamabad on Wednesday to negotiate enhanced financial assistance for Pakistan, sources said.
- The government is likely to launch a crackdown on people who defaulted on loan repayment to banks, sources said.

- The President of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry Senator Ilyas Bilour said he had asked the caretaker government to raise higher yield from agriculture tax levied last month.
- The caretaker government, under pressure from the World Bank, is likely to withdraw supply of subsidised wheat to flour mills.

- The Supreme Court, acting on a complaint by former air marshal-turned-politician Asghar Khan, asked him to file a petition against ex-army chief Aslam Beg for drawing 150 million rupees from the collapsed Mehran Bank and distributing it among politicians in the 1990 elections.
- Crystal-white sugar prices have gone up by three rupees per kilogram in the open market in the past week.
